name: Subtractive Shared Medium
topology_law: A once-continuous shared medium has a persistent local subtraction caused by an earlier human action. Two distinct people now use or occupy the same still-connected shared condition differently because the missing portion changes what each can do or where each can place themselves.
prior_action: A substantial portion of one continuous shared medium was removed/cut away earlier and remains absent now.
present_relation: Asymmetric occupation/use of one shared continuous condition; neither person is merely watching the other.
recoverable_evidence: The present subtraction has physically coherent complementary edges/continuity evidence, with enough visible residue or matching removed-state evidence to make a simpler continuous prior condition recoverable without labels.
restoration_counterfactual: Replacing/restoring the missing portion would materially restore the shared continuous condition and change both people's present use/occupation relation.

axes.causal carrier locus: missing volume inside one continuous shared medium
axes.current human relation/dependency type: asymmetric occupation/use of the same shared condition
axes.spatial relation topology: one connected field with a local interior subtraction, not a separating partition
axes.recoverable evidence type: complementary continuity break plus residual/matching subtraction evidence
axes.restoration counterfactual: restore missing medium -> common continuous condition returns

specific_prohibitions: no wall, fence, gate, barrier, channel, stepping-stone/path sequence or unit-built boundary
no crouched unit-worker plus standing observer topology
no before/after split or explanatory mark
